{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"### publish_workflow / unpublish_workflow — activate and deactivate workflows

Source: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs/blob/main/docs/connect/connect-to-n8n-mcp-server/mcp-server-tools-reference.md

These are separate top-level MCP tools (not update_workflow operations) that activate (publish) and deactivate (unpublish) a workflow for production execution.

```markdown
### publish_workflow

Available from n8n v2.12.0

Publish (activate) a workflow to make it available for production execution. This creates an active version from the current draft.

#### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `workflowId` | `string` | Yes | The ID of the workflow to publish |
| `versionId` | `string` | No | Optional version ID to publish. If not provided, publishes the current draft version. |

### unpublish_workflow

Available from n8n v2.12.0

Unpublish (deactivate) a workflow to stop production execution. The draft version is preserved and can be re-published later.

#### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `workflowId` | `string` | Yes | The ID of the workflow to unpublish |
```

--------------------------------

### Set n8n instance timezone to Europe/Berlin

Source: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs/blob/main/docs/deploy/host-n8n/configure-n8n/basic-configuration/configuration-examples/set-the-timezone.md

Use this environment variable to change the default timezone for your n8n instance. The Schedule node uses this timezone for scheduling workflows.

```bash
export GENERIC_TIMEZONE=Europe/Berlin
```

### Workflow development > Build and test workflows

Source: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs/blob/main/docs/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.webhook/workflow-development.md

When building or testing a workflow, you should use the Test webhook URL. This allows you to view incoming data directly in the editor UI, which is helpful for debugging. Before sending data, you must select 'Listen for test event' to register the webhook, which then stays active for 120 seconds. For self-hosted n8n instances on localhost, it's necessary to run n8n in tunnel mode.

--------------------------------

### Error Trigger node

Source: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs/blob/main/docs/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.errortrigger.md

The Error Trigger node is used to create error workflows. When a linked workflow fails, this node receives details about the failure and the errors, then initiates the error workflow.

--------------------------------

### Using the API

Source: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs/blob/main/docs/deploy/host-n8n/deploy-as-an-oem-integration/manage-workflows.md

To programmatically manage workflows, use the n8n API to create and activate them. First, send a POST request to the workflows endpoint with the workflow JSON to create the resource and receive a unique ID. To enable the workflow for execution, send a PATCH request to the specific workflow ID with the active property set to true. This process allows for automated deployment and configuration of workflows for different users."}],"isError":false}

tool_output.result_json:
{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"### Get current workflow execution ID

Source: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs/blob/main/docs/build/code-in-n8n/cookbook/built-in-methods-and-variables-examples/execution.md

Use this to retrieve the unique identifier for the current workflow execution. Available in both JavaScript and Python expressions.

```JavaScript
let executionId = $execution.id;
```

```Python
executionId = _execution.id
```

--------------------------------

### Node Retry and Error Handling Options

Source: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs/blob/main/docs/build/understand-workflows/workflow-components/work-with-nodes.md

Documents retry and error handling mechanisms at the node level, allowing automatic retry on failure and error workflow triggers. Critical for reliability in long-running recursive discovery services.

```markdown
Node settings for error handling and retries:

* Retry On Fail: When an execution fails, the node reruns until it succeeds.

* On Error handling options:
  - Stop Workflow: Halts the entire workflow when an error occurs
  - Continue: Proceeds to the next node despite the error, using last valid data
  - Continue (using error output): Continues workflow execution, passing error information to the next node

Error Workflows:
For each workflow, set an error workflow in Workflow Settings. It runs if an execution fails. The error workflow must start with the Error Trigger node. You can use the same error workflow for multiple workflows.

Note: HTTP Request node must handle pagination yourself. If your API call returns paginated results you must create a loop to fetch one page at a time.
```

--------------------------------

### HTTP Request node timeout option

Source: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs/blob/main/docs/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.httprequest/README.md

Documents that the timeout is in milliseconds and controls how long to wait for the server to send response headers before aborting.

```markdown
### Timeout

Use this option to set how long the node should wait for the server to send response headers (and start the response body). The node aborts requests that exceed this value for the initial response.

Enter the **Timeout** time to wait in milliseconds.
```

### 429 - The service is receiving too many requests from you > Retry on Fail

Source: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs/blob/main/docs/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.httprequest/common-issues.md

The Retry on Fail option enables the node to retry after a failed attempt. In the HTTP Request node's settings, enable "Retry on Fail" and set "Max Tries" for the number of retries. Also, configure "Wait Between Tries (ms)" to define the delay between each retry attempt.

--------------------------------

### setNodeSettings fields

Source: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs/blob/main/docs/connect/connect-to-n8n-mcp-server/mcp-server-tools-reference.md

Node execution settings include `onError` to define behavior on error (stop, continue regular, or continue error output), `retryOnFail` to enable retries, and `maxTries` (2-5 attempts) with `waitBetweenTries` (0-5000 ms) for retry configuration."}],"isError":false}
